label: PF Backlog 2
title: WG-O2: Start-from-anywhere wrapper (fetch -> pull --ff-only clean-guard -> shared token -> start) + periodic fetch-only thread
body: Part of EPIC BI-PF-0360. Source: docs/WORKER-SCHEDULER-OPERATIONS.md.

brief.problem: starting the API from an arbitrary clone risks a stale/divergent backlog; no shared token; no drift visibility.
brief.what_adds: A start wrapper that syncs develop then starts the single API, plus a periodic fetch-only thread in the API.
brief.why: Same backlog + same token regardless of which clone starts it; drift is visible.

objective: Add a start wrapper (sync + token + start) and a periodic fetch-only background thread.
acceptance_criteria: Wrapper: git fetch + git pull --ff-only origin develop, refuses if the tree is dirty, ensures PF_API_TOKEN, starts dev_server.
API startup performs one bounded git fetch before serving.
Background thread runs git fetch every N s (env-gated, default 60 dev / off in tests); fetch-only, never auto-merge.
approach: Wrapper = fetch/pull/ff(clean-guard)+token+dev_server; thread mirrors the existing state-checkpoint pattern; fetch only.
verification: dirty tree refuses; clean tree ffs; second instance still refused; thread fetches on interval.
risks: fetch racing writer (fetch-only, low); churn if interval too low.

analysis.implementation_strategy: Add a start-from-anywhere wrapper (script or endpoint extension) chaining git fetch -> pull --ff-only with clean-guard -> resolving shared token via PF_API_TOKEN -> invoking existing /api/v1/runs/start; plus a periodic fetch-only background thread.
dependency_findings: REQUIRES BI-PF-1325 for canonical PF_API_TOKEN + token_env
conflict_findings: Touches start APIs also relevant to BI-PF-1327 session model - coordinate endpoint ownership
duplication_findings: No existing start-from-anywhere wrapper in backlog
Start logic already in /api/v1/runs/start and /api/v1/portfolio/supervisor/start - extend, do not fork
analysis.rationale: Extends existing start flows; blocked only on token rename item for shared-token semantics.
assumptions: Canonical repo exists per WG-O3 plan
Shared token resolution pattern comes from BI-PF-1325
risks: git pull on dirty worktree could clobber local edits if clean-guard fails
Periodic fetch thread may conflict with worktree model (BI-PF-1327)
missing_info: Wrapper form: CLI script vs HTTP endpoint
Fetch thread interval and lifecycle owner

context_review.reason: Depends on 1325 for token; existing start APIs provide integration points.

api_impact.reason: retrofit assessment (ADR-0007): no external API consumer recorded; treated as internal until an API surface is required (then set needs_api=true with routes)
